narrative.overview:
The Teardown Lab treats structural mechanics not as static textbook diagrams, but as a live, high-velocity computational wind tunnel. The interface is an engineering flight deck: sleek computational geometry, vector heatmaps, high-density data readouts, and responsive tactile instruments. Every joint, beam, and boundary constraint is visual evidence of dynamic equilibrium.

The interface prioritizes dense scanability, instrument precision, and immediate visual feedback. Panels hover over an expansive 3D WebGL viewport like flight-director HUD overlays. Surfaces do not rely on heavy drop shadows or decorative gradients; depth is established through tonal dark-glass translucency, subtle hairline borders, and glowing active accents.
keyCharacteristics: High-Density Telemetry: Compact monospace typography, structured data tables, and inline SI engineering units.
Aerodynamic Vector Heatmaps: ANSYS-standard stress contour gradients communicating structural strain.
Glass Cockpit Layering: Translucent slate backdrops with backdrop blur and slate-700 hairline borders.
Tactile Instrument Controls: Custom micro-stepper up/down arrow buttons, immediate slider feedback, and responsive mode toggles.

rules.name: The Telemetry Rarity Rule
rules.body: Glowing colored accents (cyan, amber, red) must never exceed 15% of any surface area. The deep slate neutral canvas provides the high-contrast negative space that allows critical warnings to command instant cognitive attention.

rules.name: The Tabular Number Rule
rules.body: All numerical readouts, coordinate listings, forces, and safety factors must render with monospaced figures (tabular-nums / font-mono) to prevent visual jitter during live simulation scrubs.

rules.name: The Hairline Separation Rule
rules.body: Never use diffuse ambient shadows to separate adjacent UI elements. Separation must be achieved strictly through 1px border contrast (border-slate-800 to border-slate-700) and slight tone steps.

dos: Do format all calculated numerical outputs with strict rounding precision (.toFixed(1) or .toFixed(2)) and pair them with standard SI units.
Do maintain a minimum contrast ratio of 7:1 for telemetry readouts against dark backgrounds using slate-100 or slate-200.
Do use custom NumericStepperInput components for numeric parameters, preserving the styled SVG up/down arrows.
Do ensure HUD panels use backdrop-blur and translucent backgrounds so the underlying 3D simulation remains visible.
Do isolate destructive actions (TEARDOWN TO FAILURE) with explicit red visual semantics.
donts: Don't use generic browser default number input spinners with blue OS outlines.
Don't use saturated bright backgrounds or light themes; the platform is strictly a dark-mode flight deck.
Don't introduce heavy multi-layer drop shadows (shadow-2xl blur > 40px) that muddy the sharp instrument aesthetic.
Don't allow UI panels to overlap the 3D model without clear z-index layering and collapsible panel triggers.
Don't hide mathematical formulas behind black-box outputs; always expose governing equations alongside live calculated values.
